lines.text: In 2025, 79% of stock-picking pros lost to an index.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, seventy-nine percent of stock-picking pros lost to an index.

lines.text: That's big US stock funds, beaten by a basket that never picks.
lines.say: That's big US stock funds, beaten by a basket that never picks anything.

scene.label: Active large-cap US funds that trailed the S&P 500 in 2025

lines.text: Picking stocks = hunting one perfect acorn. Index fund = the whole basket.
lines.say: Picking stocks is hunting for one perfect acorn. An index fund just grabs the whole basket.

lines.text: Not one bad year: most pros lost every year from 2021 to 2025.
lines.say: And it's not one bad year. Most pros lost every single year from twenty twenty-one to twenty twenty-five.

scene.title: Active big funds that lost to the S&P 500

lines.text: First half of 2026, with conditions that favored pickers: 67% still trailed.
lines.say: Even in the first half of twenty twenty-six, when conditions favored stock pickers, sixty-seven percent still trailed.

scene.headline: Early 2026: 67% of big active funds trailed the index

lines.text: A big reason is fees: on $10,000 in 2025, about $64 for active stock funds versus $5 for index stock funds.
lines.say: A big reason is fees. On ten thousand dollars in twenty twenty-five, active stock funds averaged about sixty-four dollars. Index stock funds, about five.

lines.text: The squirrel pays its acorn guide every year, whether the hunt works or not.
lines.say: The squirrel pays its acorn guide every year, whether the hunt works or not.

lines.text: Some pickers do win. The hard part is knowing which ones, ahead of time.
lines.say: Some pickers do win. The hard part is knowing which ones ahead of time, and the odds aren't great.

post.title: Why 79% of Pro Stock Pickers Lost to an Index Fund
post.ig:
In 2025, 79% of stock-picking pros lost to an index.
Active large-cap US funds that trailed the S&P 500: 85% in 2021, 51% in 2022, 60% in 2023, 65% in 2024, 79% in 2025.
In the first half of 2026, 67% still trailed.
Average 2025 fee on $10,000: about $64 for active stock funds vs $5 for index stock funds.
Sources: S&P Dow Jones Indices SPIVA U.S. Year-End 2025 and Mid-Year 2026, U.S. Persistence Scorecard Year-End 2025; ICI Trends in Expenses and Fees of Funds, 2025.
